summary: Northwood Lighthouse on Grand Lake St. Marys, Ohio: a 1923 two-thirds-scale Eddystone replica on private land, closed to visitors.

lens.note: Reportedly from a lighthouse off Cuba (LighthouseFriends). The community history says fifth-order.

access.note: On private property and closed to visitors. Best viewed from the water or from Northwood Drive (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Tower built by developer Bill Jasperson as a promotional 'drawing card' for the Northwood subdivision. Two-thirds-scale Eddystone replica.
The community history gives 1925 for the tower's construction; LighthouseFriends and Rowlett give 1923.
The community history gives the Sommers family as owners from 1932; LighthouseFriends says Frank Sommers bought the development in the 1930s.
Lighthouse offered for sale at $50,000, with an easement across neighboring land for access (LighthouseFriends).
Community history gives 1975 as the end of the Sommers ownership and the start of a later owner's term.
A later steward restored the tradition by relighting the beacon (community history).
Lake Improvement Association restored and reactivated the lighthouse (Rowlett's directory).

notes_for_editor: Checked 2026-10-27 against the cached LighthouseFriends page, the Welcome to Northwood history page, the Rowlett directory (ibiblio) Ohio page, and the USLHS place record. SCOPE QUESTION FOR THE OWNER: the USLHS archive classes this as a Private (Faux) Lighthouse, not an active aid. LighthouseFriends says it ran as a seasonal aid under a government license. DESIGN section 1 excludes decorative lighthouses that never served as an aid to navigation; the owner should decide whether it stays in scope before publication. Disagreements, all stated in the story or left open: build date 1923 (LighthouseFriends, Rowlett) vs 1925 (community history); height fifty feet (LighthouseFriends, Rowlett) vs seventy feet (community history); lens from a Cuban lighthouse (LighthouseFriends) vs fifth-order (community history); land: 'private property' (LighthouseFriends visitor note, Rowlett) vs lease rights to state-owned land (LighthouseFriends 1972 price note); ownership: Sommers 1932-1975 (community history) vs an offer for sale in 1972 (LighthouseFriends); reactivation: Lake Improvement Association in 2020 (Rowlett) vs a private steward relighting in 2012 (community history). The community history is the only source for the 2012 relighting and for the Sommers and McKirnan owners; the 2012 steward is not named in the story (a private individual). Owners named in the story: Bill Jasperson (developer, 1923) and Frank Sommers (public role; ownership ended 1972-75). Spelling: LighthouseFriends prints Jasperson; the community history prints Jaspersen. The queue's status note says no usable position; LighthouseFriends' coordinates (40.543536, -84.481395) match the OSM record, so the note looks stale. Chronicling America searches for 1923-25 found no Ohio hits. Corpus searches of the Lighthouse Board, Commissioner and Bulletin reports found no Ohio entry (the 'Grand Lake' hits are Louisiana). NRHP nomination 82003614 is not digitised at npgallery (placeholder PDF), so it could not be read. Thin evidence: four sources, all community, directory or archive records, so the story is short with no headings. No photos mirrored.
